identificationModule.briefTitle: Comparison of Olanzapine and Metoclopramide For Treatment Of bReakThrough Emesis
identificationModule.officialTitle: Efficacy of Olanzapine in Break-through Emesis After Prophylaxis With Dexamethasone, 5-HT3 Receptor Antagonists and Aprepitant Compared to Metoclopramide

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This trial is designed to evaluate olanzapine compared to the metoclopramide in the treatment of break through emesis after prophylaxis with dexamethasone, 5-HT 3 receptor antagonists and aprepitant in patients receiving chemotherapy. Efficacy will be assessed using a modified MASCC questionaire with a visual analog scale.

keywords: break through emesis after prophylaxis with dexamethasone, 5-HT 3RA and aprepitant

primaryOutcomes.description: no vomitus, no further rescue medication, nausea \< 25mm on the visual analog scale (VAS) or reduction on the VAS of \>50%

secondaryOutcomes.measure: change in urinary excretion of 5 hydroxy indole acetic acid

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* break through emesis after prophylaxis with dexamethasone, 5-HT 3 receptor antagonists and aprepitant in patients receiving chemotherapy defined as vomitus or nausea\>25mm on VAS
* signed IC

Exclusion Criteria:

* psychiatric disorders
* drug abuse
* pregnancy
* high dose chemotherapy
* treatment with other antiemetic drugs

locations.facility: Martin-Luther-University Halle-Wittenberg, Department for Oncology and Hematology, Ernst-Grube-Strasse 40
